title: Sundown Fabrics shipping ops LLM scratchpad
content:
Meeting capture: Sundown Fabrics — Shipping Ops LLM POC (10/28/2025)
Participants: Priya Rao (Head of Logistics, Sundown), Tom Wexler (SRE), Ishaan Mehra (ML eng), Clara Nguyen (Redwood SE), Marco Diaz (Redwood Solutions)

Goal summary:
- Replace rule-heavy routing notes with assisted, context-aware dispatch suggestions generated at time of pick/pack.
- Fast single-turn suggestions (operator UI) + on-demand multi-step reasoning for exception cases.
- Keep PII off-hosted model logs; prefer Private deployment in their AWS account (VPC) or Dedicated if timeline demands.

Business metrics & targets mentioned:
- Peak throughput ~40k orders/hr (~11.1 orders/sec sustained; optimistic bursts to 200 req/s at 5-minute windows).
- Latency target for UI inline suggestions: <= 150ms p50, <= 300ms p95 ideally.
- Cost target: keep inference spend under $0.10 per 1k orders during pilot (they will benchmark).

Technical constraints/gotchas called out by client:
- Many shipping labels include long free-text carrier notes and customer comments; median order tokenized length ~900 tokens, heavy tail to 5k+ tokens for returns history. We need truncation/summary pipeline before hits the model.
- Carrier webhook payloads mutate after initial creation (address corrections). KV cache invalidation needs to be aware of event stream.
- PII compliance: customer wants no raw customer addresses in logs. Must confirm Redwood Private/KMS + DPA + redaction pipeline.
- Interoperability: they have an in-house Go microservice stack, gRPC front, want a simple REST shim or SDK example.
- Edge case: label OCR outputs are messy; attached images often carry OCR hallucinations that can trip prompt parsing.

Redwood product options discussed (notes from call):
- Preferred: Redwood Private (VPC) with customer-managed KMS, pin model versions, default canary rollouts for updates.
- Alternative: Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) if they prefer Redwood-managed infra to move quickly; tradeoff is sending PII to Redwood-managed infra which they are cautious about.
- Runtime features we'll lean on: prefix/KV caching for repeated address lookups, model variant fallback (smaller model for heuristics), batching for non-interactive post-processing jobs.

Immediate technical risks to validate:
- Tokenization blowup for return histories -> need summarization lambda before prompt. Decide whether summarization runs on Redwood or in-client.
- Live cache invalidation: if they rely on evented address corrections, we must add a webhook -> invalidate cache hook (SLA dependent).
- Prompt injection from carrier-supplied free text (they run third-party carriers). Must strip commands/URLs and normalize input.

Sample system / user prompt (working):
System: You are an operations assistant that summarizes the shipping-relevant fields and suggests the best dispatch option. Always remove or mask customer PII (names, addresses, phone numbers) from your output. If uncertain, ask for clarification instead of guessing.
User: Order #34522: items 3x sweater, 1x hat. Delivery history: "left at front door, customer complaint: wrong size; customer note: call before delivery". Carrier notes: "Left at side 8am per homeowner request; rescheduled by carrier 2025-09-12"
Expected assistant output (short): 1) Masked address + best dispatch option: local same-day partner (cost 1.2x) — reason: prior failed delivery; 2) Recommended message to customer: "We will attempt delivery between 12–4PM; please confirm"; 3) Flags: escalate to exceptions if address mismatch detected.

Proposed pilot architecture (sketch):
- In-client preprocessor (Go) strips PII, runs lightweight summarizer for long histories -> calls Redwood Private endpoint pinned to model v1.2.
- Redwood runtime: Dedicated pool with 4x A10-equivalent GPUs behind a dedicated route, autoscale buffer for bursts, KV cache for recent orders keyed by order_id hash.
- Observability: route-level dashboards in Redwood Console for latency/cost per route, prompt-level eval capture for quality regressions.

Open questions (need answers from Sundown):
- Can they provide 2k sample orders with redacted PHI for eval set? (Ishaan to confirm)
- Do they have an internal KMS/AWS key they must use? If yes, get key ARN and key rotation policy.
- Which legal docs do they need: SOC2 + DPA + data residency statement? Priya to confirm requirement list.

Action items / next steps (owner + due):
- Clara: send annotated POC proposal + cost worksheet for both Private (customer VPC) and Dedicated options. Due 2025-11-03.
- Marco: draft summarization lambda prototype (Python) and example token reduction stats on sample subset. Due 2025-11-10.
- Sundown (Ishaan): share first 500 redacted orders + sample carrier webhook payloads (masked) for schema validation. Due 2025-11-07.
- Legal/CS: surface DPA + SOC2 cert to client, confirm KMS requirements. Assigned to Anika. Due 2025-11-06.
- Create JIRA SPD-4821 to track infra setup, include tasks for cache invalidation hook, KMS integration, and example Go SDK snippet.

Notes to self (SE):
- Need a short demo showing latency at 150ms p50 with small-context prompt; prepare benchmark script using Redwood local client.
- Build prompt set focusing on: address normalization, exception escalation, customer-facing templated messages. Will include negative test cases (prompt injection, OCR garbage).
- Consider recommending a hybrid: Private for interactive UI flows (low-latency), Dedicated for nightly batch re-ranking and analytics to reduce cost.

Quick risks + mitigations:
- Risk: PII leakage -> Mitigation: client-side redaction + server-side log scrubbing + contract DPA + allow exclude-from-logs flag on requests.
- Risk: Large token orders blow budget -> Mitigation: summarization pre-step + prefix caching + model truncation policy.

Rough cost sketch (ballpark, for proposal):
- Private (customer VPC, pilot): setup + infra + support: $12k/month + one-time onboarding $8k.
- Dedicated (4 GPU reserved): ~$18k/month (includes reserved capacity, autoscale buffer) — exact depends on GPU type.
(Do not quote until finance review)

Later thoughts: Could explore a small on-prem inference gateway (air-gapped) if legal says no cross-account traffic — raise with product/privates.

End of scratchpad.

Unresolved: confirm whether Sundown will accept masked sample orders in S3 or will only share via secure portal.
